facts.statement: Ajnabia is the first definitive hadrosaur discovered in Africa.
facts.quote: It is the first definitive hadrosaur from Africa

facts.statement: Ajnabia fossils were recovered from Late Maastrichtian strata in the phosphate mines at Sidi Chennane, Khouribga Province, Morocco.
facts.quote: Ajnabia was recovered from the Late Maastrichtian strata of the phosphate mines at Sidi Chennane, in Khouribga Province, Morocco.

facts.statement: The preserved incomplete maxilla of Ajnabia measures 15.6 cm in length, though its front and top edges are broken.
facts.quote: As preserved, the incomplete maxilla is 15.6 cm long, with the anterior (toward the front) and dorsal (toward the top) edges broken.

facts.statement: When complete, the maxilla of Ajnabia may have been around 19 to 20 cm long.
facts.quote: When complete, it may have been around 19 - 20 cm long.

facts.statement: Twenty-three tooth sockets are preserved in the maxilla of Ajnabia.
facts.quote: Twenty-three alveoli (tooth sockets) are preserved in the maxilla.

facts.statement: Ajnabia was a small animal approximately 3 meters long.
facts.quote: Era un animal pequeño de aproximadamente 3 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Examination of Ajnabia's teeth and jaw reveals it belonged to the Lambeosaurinae subfamily, characterized by duck-bills and elaborate bone crests on their heads.
facts.quote: El examen de los dientes y la mandíbula de Ajnabia revela que pertenecía a la familia Lambeosaurinae, una subfamilia de dinosaurios con pico de pato y crestas óseas elaboradas en la cabeza.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ajnabia was found in the phosphates of the Ouled Abdoun Basin in north-central Morocco.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MHNM KHG 222, was recovered from the phosphates of the Ouled Abdoun Basin of north-central Morocco.

facts.statement: In a 2021 analysis, Longrich et al. recovered Ajnabia as the sister taxon to Blasisaurus, a hadrosaur from Spain.
facts.quote: In their 2021 phylogenetic analysis, Longrich et al. recovered Ajanbia as the sister taxon to Blasisaurus, a hadrosaur from the Arén Formation of Spain.

facts.statement: In a 2022 analysis, Ramírez-Velasco placed Ajnabia as the sister taxon to Pararhabdodon within the Tsintaosaurini, rather than in the Arenysaurini clade.
facts.quote: In a separate analysis in 2022, Ramírez-Velasco did not recover an arenysaurin clade; instead, these taxa were distributed throughout the Lambeosaurinae. Ajnabia was found to be the sister taxon to Pararhabdodon within the Tsintaosaurini

facts.statement: Ajnabia is classified within the tribe Arenysaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Arenysaurini

facts.statement: Ajnabia belongs to the tribe Arenysaurini.
facts.quote: Es el primer hadrosáurido definitivo de África y pertenece a la tribu Arenysaurini.

facts.statement: Possible means of dispersal for Ajnabia include swimming, drifting, or rafting on floating debris or vegetation.
facts.quote: Possible means of dispersal include swimming, drifting, or rafting (wherein animals are transported on top of floating debris or vegetation).

facts.statement: While rafting is unlikely for a large animal, it is considered possible that young hadrosaurs could have been transported this way.
facts.quote: Rafting is considered unlikely for a large animal, but it's considered possible that young hadrosaurs could be transported in this way.

facts.statement: It is debated whether intermittent land connections could have served as a means of dispersal for Ajnabia, though oceanic dispersal is favored.
facts.quote: Intermittent land connections as a means of dispersal could not be ruled out.

facts.statement: Ajnabia is remarkable because it challenges the assumption that hadrosaurs could not reach Africa, which was isolated by water during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Africa was isolated by water from the rest of the world during the Cretaceous, such that hadrosaurs were assumed to have been unable to reach the continent.

facts.statement: Ajnabia was discovered in the Ouled Abdoun basin in Morocco and named by Longrich et al. in 2020.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la cuenca Ouled Abdoun, Marruecos y nombrado por Longrich et al., 2020.

facts.statement: The name Ajnabia comes from the Arabic word for "stranger" or "traveler," referring to the dinosaur lineage that migrated to Africa from elsewhere.
facts.quote: El nombre Ajnabia deriva del árabe ajnabi, أجنبي,que significa "viajero" o "extranjero", refiriéndose al animal como parte de un linaje de dinosaurios que emigró a África desde otros lugares.

facts.statement: The type species, A. odysseus, is named after the Greek hero and legendary sailor Odysseus.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, A. odysseus, se refiere al héroe griego y legendario navegante Odiseo.

facts.statement: The holotype was recovered from phosphates in the Ouled Abdoun basin in north-central Morocco.
facts.quote: El holotipo se recuperó de los fosfatos de la cuenca de Ouled Abdoun en el centro-norte de Marruecos.

facts.statement: The phosphate environment where the fossil was found was a near-shore marine habitat populated by sharks, fish, mosasaurs, and other marine reptiles.
facts.quote: Los fosfatos son un entorno marino cercano a la costa, habitado por tiburones, peces, mosasaurios y otros reptiles marinos.

facts.statement: Ajnabia lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Late Maastrichtian, approximately 1 million years before the K-Pg boundary and the Chicxulub asteroid impact.
facts.quote: Estos dinosaurios habrían vivido en el Cretácico tardío, Maastrichtiano tardío, aproximadamente 1 millón de años antes del límite K-Pg y el impacto del asteroide Chicxulub que acabó con los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Ajnabia is a member of Lambeosaurinae and specifically of Arenysaurini, a clade previously known only in Europe.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético sugiere que Ajnabia es un miembro de Lambeosaurinae y específicamente un miembro de Arenysaurini, un clado conocido sólo en Europa.

facts.statement: Ajnabia belongs to the parent group Arenysaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Arenysaurini

facts.statement: Ajnabia is classified within the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Ajnabia belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Ajnabia lived from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers propose that Lambeosaurinae dispersed into North Africa via oceanic dispersal, with hadrosaurs swimming or floating between Europe and North Africa.
facts.quote: se propuso que la dispersión de Lambeosaurinae en el norte de África probablemente se produjo a través de la dispersión oceánica, con hadrosaurios nadando o flotando entre Europa y el norte de África.

facts.statement: While oceanic dispersal is the leading theory, intermittent land connections were not entirely ruled out as a dispersal mechanism for hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Si bien la dispersión oceánica se había considerado previamente para la distribución de los hadrosaurios europeos, no se podían descartar las conexiones terrestres intermitentes como medio de dispersión.

facts.statement: Possible dispersal methods included swimming, drifting, or rafting on floating debris or vegetation.
facts.quote: Los posibles medios de dispersión incluyen la natación, la deriva o el rafting, donde los animales son transportados sobre escombros flotantes o vegetación.

facts.statement: Rafting is considered unlikely for large animals, but it is possible that young hadrosaurs could have been transported this way.
facts.quote: El rafting se considera poco probable para un animal grande, pero se considera posible que los hadrosaurios jóvenes pudieran ser transportados de esta manera.

facts.statement: While Laurasia is characterized by tyrannosaurs and ornithischian herbivores, Gondwana is dominated by titanosaurs and abelisaurids, as seen in Morocco.
facts.quote: Mientras que Laurasia se caracteriza por tiranosáuridos, ornitisquios y celurosaurios herbívoros, Gondwana está dominada por titanosaurios y abelisaurios, como se ve en Marruecos.

facts.statement: The endemism in Gondwanan faunas is explained by the fragmentation of the supercontinent into increasingly distant landmasses, causing ancestral faunas to diverge.
facts.quote: Este endemismo se explica por la fragmentación del antiguo supercontinente de Gondwana en masas de tierra cada vez más distantes, lo que llevó a que las faunas ancestralmente vinculadas de diferentes continentes del sur se volvieran distintas.
